page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highcpu-64 is an ARM64-based virtual server engineered for high-density compute workloads. The machine configuration provides 64 dedicated vCPUs alongside 128.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of exactly 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This architecture targets multi-threaded workloads that demand significant raw processing capacity without requiring large in-memory caches.

Hardware provisioning for this instance excludes integrated acceleration and internal disk drives. The server features zero attached GPUs, directing all platform resources to standard instruction processing. Local storage is designated as None, indicating that the instance does not provide bundled local NVMe disks; all persistent and temporary data must reside on network-attached storage volumes. Additionally, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned directly to the instance, requiring standard network routing or external IP assignment configurations.

From an operational tradeoff and efficiency perspective, the dedicated ARM64 core allocation delivers predictable execution without hyper-threading overhead. The lower memory-per-core footprint maximizes CPU density, avoiding the overhead of paying for unutilized memory capacity when running core-heavy applications. Google Cloud Platform n4a-highcpu-64 fits containerized microservices, distributed batch processing, parallel source code compilation, video transcoding, and horizontal web serving tiers optimized for native ARM64 instruction sets.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highcpu-64 is a dedicated ARM64 compute instance engineered for processing-heavy workloads requiring high core density. Equipped with 64 dedicated ARM64 virtual CPUs and 128 GB of system memory, the instance delivers a fixed compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero integrated GPUs, focusing all capacity on primary CPU throughput. In addition, the instance includes no local storage volumes, requiring system administrators to utilize remote persistent storage disks for file systems and databases. The absence of bundled physical NVMe drives and dedicated accelerator hardware optimizes infrastructure resource density for organizations running scale-out applications. With its 64 dedicated ARM cores, n4a-highcpu-64 is well aligned for large-scale software compilation, batch processing pipelines, web serving clusters, continuous integration workers, and containerized microservices operating on native ARM architectures.
